r3_note: Medi's lines 44:57-47:22 are missing (only Amal's side of the go-home command drill); D11-D13 are kept low/medium from her side. 09:47 and 03:57 each hold two real pieces (vocab + grammar) that the readers paired crosswise. No agreed-row challenges.

rows.medi_said: I, I removed is إيديت? ... It's بعيد, right? بعيد.
rows.why: He knows بقيم (sheet: 'i remove / take away | Ana ba2eem | أنا بقيم') but could not make the past; Amal gave إمت and he took it ('بعيم, that's right. So إمت'). بعيد is the engine/S4 for بعيم, so tier 2 not tier 1.
rows.r3_why: Same slip both readers; known verb, wrong form -> tier 2.

rows.medi_said: Do you guys use enough كافية? Is, uh، is this an Arabic word or no?
rows.why: He asked whether كافية is used; Amal supplied بكفي - a didn't-know.

rows.medi_said: كل اليوم مش-- uh، ما عندي بكافية وقت.
rows.why: He is describing his usual days (no time for exercise, family): every day = كل يوم; كل اليوم = the whole day. Could be read 'all day', so low.
rows.english: every day I don't have enough time
rows.r3_why: Plausible A11 let-pass; low because 'all day' also fits.

rows.medi_said: ما عندي بكافية وقت.
rows.why: The 'enough' word describes وقت and goes after it; Amal's recast puts it after the noun.
rows.r3_why: Order slip at the same moment as D4; A7 (describer after the noun) fits better than C9.

rows.medi_said: Yeah، راح يسعد. Yeah، راح يسعدني. [unintelligible] It
rows.why: يسعد means make happy; he meant 'it will help (me)' and Amal gave يساعد. (He self-fixed أسعدني to يسعدني before her; the fixed version is what she corrected.)

rows.medi_said: بفكر إنه كل إشي بيحر-- كل إشي بيحر-- بيحرك.
rows.amal_said: بيت حرك. ... لا، بيت is you getting moved. So كل إشي gets moved.
rows.why: بيحرك = moves something; for 'everything is moving' Amal gave بيتحرك and explained the t- form is getting moved.
rows.english: I think everything is moving (so fast).

rows.medi_said: بدك، بدك المطر؟
rows.why: He meant 'do you like the rain?' (she just said it was nice); بدك = want. She answered with بحب and he took it ('بـ-بتحب، yeah').

rows.medi_said: الفلسطينيين، uh، ناخد المطر؟ المي؟
rows.why: Subject is the Palestinians (they) but the verb is we-form ناخد without b-; Amal only asked what he meant.
rows.r3_why: Both readers wrote both rows at 09:47, paired crosswise; D7 = the B18 person slip.

rows.medi_said: الفلسطينيين، uh، ناخد المطر؟ المي؟
rows.why: 'Take the rain' for 'collect rainwater': Amal could not follow (كيف يعني؟) and he switched to English 'Do they collect rainwater?'. Right verb is my reading.
rows.r3_why: D8 = the vocab piece of the same moment.

rows.medi_said: أنا جربت بس الـ set، uh, يخرب، uh, يخرب-- يخرب-- يخرب؟
rows.why: Telling what happened (the card set broke) needs past; he said present يخرب and asked, Amal gave past خربه; he then said خربوا 'That's right'.
rows.english: I tried, but the set broke (it).

rows.medi_said: بنت به. Uh, بنت به. Yeah, بنت, بنت به is to, to take care of something.
rows.amal_said: Actually، بنتبه is more like pay attention.
rows.right: بنتبه = pay attention (ديري بالك = take care)
rows.why: Asked for 'pay attention' vs 'take care', he gave انتبه for take care; Amal said it means pay attention and he said 'Oh, whoops'.
rows.english: Which word means take care / pay attention.

rows.medi_said: Great. تمارنتي
rows.why: She asked for a command; he said a past-tense 'you (f) exercised' form, Amal said 'أمر' (command) and he changed to تمارني.

rows.medi_said: بيجيب اللي. ... بيجيب اللي أي. Yeah.
rows.amal_said: جبيلي إياه. Why did you put be؟
rows.why: A command has no b-; Amal gave جيبلي إياه and asked why he put the b-.

rows.medi_said: Trump hadeekna, tehekna.
rows.why: 'Fool someone' is ضحك على; he said hadeekna (made us laugh) and Amal repeated ضحك until he said tehekalayna.

rows.medi_said: Hadik al-dawla, uh, is, uh, biddik jibal.
rows.why: 'If you like mountains' came without el-; Amal recast الجبال (and confirmed plural جبال, singular جبل). He asked 'what did I say?'.

rows.medi_said: Surprise. It's, uh, I don't know how to say surprise.
rows.why: He said he did not know 'surprise'; Amal supplied مفاجأة.
rows.english: Keep quiet about the party because it's a surprise.

rows.medi_said: [his line missing from the transcript]
rows.amal_said: it's a wrong form. Let's go back home. La la. Right verb, but wrong command form. ... We said it's a double W. So rawahi.
rows.wrong: (wrong command form of بروح, not transcribed)
rows.why: After 'عطيني كمان جملة' (46:03) his new sentence had the wrong command form; Amal said 'Right verb, but wrong command form' and gave rawahi. A second slip after D11, in a new sentence.
rows.r3_why: Explicit no in a new sentence; separate from D11.

rows.medi_said: حوالي، uh, تيس-- ... Would I say تيس على تيس؟
rows.why: Clock time needs el- (على التسع); he said تيس bare and Amal recast twice, he repeated على التيس.

rows.medi_said: [speaking foreign language] على. And that one is logical.
rows.why: 'Keep quiet about' is اسكت عن; he gave على and Amal said عن.

rows.medi_said: Uh, khafi, khafi.
rows.why: For 'scare me' he used khafi (get scared); Amal said 'No' and he moved to the doubled-middle خوفني.

held_one_reader.medi_said: اليوم أنا إمت، uh, Instagram و لوب، uh، ألعاب، uh، من تلفوني
held_one_reader.why: The specific games on his phone are known things and need el-; Amal let it pass (her own 05:06 line says والـ ألعاب).
held_one_reader.english: today I removed Instagram and the games from my phone

held_one_reader.why: بكافية is a made-up blend of كافية and the بكفي she had just given at 03:44; Amal re-said it as وقت بكفي.
held_one_reader.r3_why: Both pieces are real at this moment: the non-word (vocab, this row) and the word order (D5). Tier 1 = non-word.

held_one_reader.medi_said: Is it لا? I don't remember this one.
held_one_reader.why: Quizzed on what بنتبه takes, he answered لـ; Amal gave على ('الاتنين بياخدوا على') and he took it ('علا. Okay. Both.'). Same kind of quiz answer as agreed A7 (بتدرب لا؟ -> على).
held_one_reader.r3_why: Quiz answer she corrected, consistent with agreed A7.

held_one_reader.why: He could not find the verb for 'practice' (offered ماران, asked if it was a new verb, said أنا نسيت) and Amal supplied بتدرب; he said 'Oh, that's right'.

held_one_reader.medi_said: أنا لازم أتدرب، uh, ستي ... بتدرب لا؟
held_one_reader.amal_said: وبتدرب شو، شو بتدرب بتاخد؟ ... A preposition. ... على.
held_one_reader.why: He left out the preposition after أتدرب; Amal prompted ('A preposition'), he guessed لا, and she supplied على.
held_one_reader.english: I have to practice the set.

held_one_reader.amal_said: حرب. جدد. We didn't learn the plural for حرب. ... حروب.
held_one_reader.why: He meant 'no new wars' with the singular; Amal said they had not learned the plural and supplied حروب (and جدد) - a didn't-know, tier 0. jadeed->jadeeda was his self-fix.
held_one_reader.r3_why: Not-yet-learned plural = didn't-know (vocab-A tier 0), not an A9 slip.

held_one_reader.amal_said: سافري. ... Yeah، cuz you said it سافري. You should say سافري.
held_one_reader.why: He said the command with a short a; Amal recast سافري and told him he said it wrong, he agreed ('I said it wrong ... Oh, it's long A'). Vowel length has its own bucket (F2), so it is filed, not S4-dropped.
held_one_reader.r3_why: Voiced fix he accepted; F2 exists for vowel length.

held_one_reader.medi_said: imta barawe min safar, um, when are you gonna leave from your trip?
held_one_reader.why: Amal's sentence was 'min el safar'; he said it back without el- and she only fixed the meaning ('Gonna come back from your trip').
held_one_reader.english: when are you coming back from the trip?
held_one_reader.r3_why: Let-pass el- drop; low (he is translating her line).

held_one_reader.medi_said: [his lines 44:57-47:22 are missing from the transcript]
held_one_reader.amal_said: Baraw-barawih. What do you think? It's a double something, but not R. ... it's already indicated that's like rawahi.
held_one_reader.wrong: barawih (command of بروح, engine did not write his line)
held_one_reader.why: Amal echoes his barawih (a present form for 'go home!') and coaches the double-w command rawahi; his own line is missing, so low.
held_one_reader.r3_why: Real coached command fix; transcript hole -> low.

held_one_reader.amal_said: If I want to say the beit, I would have to say to the home. So what's the to part? Ala el beit. So rawahi ala el beit badri.
held_one_reader.why: Amal asked for the 'to' part and gave على البيت - he left the preposition out; his line is missing, so low.
held_one_reader.r3_why: Distinct piece (preposition) from D11's command form; low, transcript hole.

held_one_reader.medi_said: Because you forgot your keys, so ashan nisti ma-- uh... But what is it for you feminine? Is it nisti?
held_one_reader.amal_said: Mm. So you forgot. It's one of the irregulars. ... Nseeti because, because you is nseed.
held_one_reader.why: Past 'you (f) forgot' is irregular نسيتي; he used nisti in his sentence and Amal gave nseeti, which he repeated.

held_one_reader.medi_said: أنا برجع، uh, [speaking foreign language] right?
held_one_reader.why: Amal supplied من الgym and he answered 'Oh, you said من؟ أنا برجع من الجيم' - he had left من out; his words are partly untranscribed.
held_one_reader.english: I come back from the gym
held_one_reader.r3_why: His 'Oh, you said من؟' shows he lacked it.

held_one_reader.medi_said: Uh, like quiet about how much it costs? I thought hat was costs.
held_one_reader.wrong: quiet about how much it costs
held_one_reader.why: He read حق in her ما بسكت عن حقي as 'cost'; Amal said no and led him to 'rights'. This is his reading of her Arabic, so mode listening.
held_one_reader.english: I won't keep quiet about my rights
held_one_reader.r3_why: Real misread of her Arabic; filed as listening.

held_one_reader.medi_said: So a la, a la. A la i?
held_one_reader.why: The command of بقلق needs the i- prefix (more than three letters); he tried 'a la i', Amal gave اقلقي twice and he took it ('it is more than three. So a, it la i').

held_one_reader.amal_said: بلاش. خوفني، yes. مش إي. Did you put an إي؟
held_one_reader.why: A doubled-middle verb's command takes no i-; Amal said 'مش إي' and he admitted 'I did', then said khawafni. Engine dropped the i-. Separate from agreed A16 (wrong verb khafi, B12).
